approach: Add a hold as an append-only per-job record (`athena.hold/1`, `<job>/hold-<n>.json`, state `held` or `released`; highest `n` wins). `JobRecords::on_hold()` is true when the job is still queued and its latest hold record is `held`. `RealSteps::entry_of` copies that into a new `PlanEntry.on_hold` flag. `Plan::build_with`, which every plan builder calls (`build`, `build_capped`, `build_improving`), refuses an `on_hold` entry before anything else, with reason "on hold" and an empty `missing`. Anything that depends on it is held through the existing dependency-hold loop. `Drain::prepare` skips reading a held item, and `batches_for` already drops everything in `plan.refused`, so drain never dispatches it at any priority. `athena plan` already prints refused items with an empty `missing` as a `held` line. `Athena::set_hold` and `release_hold` copy `set_priority`. `athena hold` and `athena release` dispatch through commands.rs. Status shows "on hold". Priority is untouched.

decisions.choice: Enforce the hold in `Plan::build_with` through a new `PlanEntry.on_hold: bool` (serde skipped when false). The hold reason is built in plan.rs.
decisions.reason: The plan is the one place that decides what drain dispatches: `Drain::prepare` builds it, `athena plan` prints it, and `batches_for` (drain.rs:3034) dispatches only its groups. Holding there makes `Plan::build` alone never order a held item, so the unit test covers all four priorities, and dependents are held by the existing loop (plan.rs:700-726) with no new logic. `PlanEntry::bare` plus `..bare` spreads keep most literals compiling.

rejected.option: A new `Steps::on_hold` method merged into `Drain::prepare`'s `held` map (drain.rs:2302), the way a paused line is held.
rejected.why: The rule would live only in the CLI crate, so `Plan::build` would still order a held item. It would also need a stub override and a separate dependents loop; the paused-line loop at drain.rs:2313 words its reason as 'its line is paused'.
They would not appear in `athena plan`, which the request requires, and `athena status` would lose them.

rejected.option: Lower the item's priority, or add a fifth 'held' priority level.
rejected.why: This is the failure the request describes. The request forbids tying hold to priority, and a new level would change how `Priority::parse`, the caps and the order work, all out of scope.

decisions.choice: Hold state is a separate record type, `HoldRecord { job, n, at, state: held|released }`, at `<job>/hold-<n>.json`. `n` is numbered per job and the highest wins, as for priority records. No reason text.
decisions.reason: Records are append-only (`PriorityRecord` doc, records.rs:520-523), so a release is a later record, not an edit. A separate type leaves `athena.priority/1` and its validator (PRIORITY_LEVELS) alone, so hold stays independent of priority. The request left a reason text optional ('a short optional text'); omitting it is the smallest design.

rejected.why: It changes an existing schema (`deny_unknown_fields`, records.rs:524), and the latest-record-wins rule would tie hold and priority together, so setting a priority would implicitly release the hold.

rejected.option: A free-text hold reason shown in plan.
rejected.why: Not needed to meet the request, and it adds validation and a longer display line.

decisions.choice: `JobRecords::on_hold()` requires `state() == Queued` as well as a latest `held` record. `set_hold` refuses a job that is not queued or is already held. `release_hold` refuses a job that is not held.
decisions.reason: Mirrors `set_priority`, which allows a priority only on a queued request (reading.rs:1008). A hold left on a job that later got read (`athena go`) can then never block that job's retry, which drain works as an interrupted or proposed item.

rejected.option: Let the hold apply to any job state.
rejected.why: A stale hold would silently stop a retry of an interrupted job that the operator can no longer release, since release is checked against queued state.

decisions.choice: In `Plan::build_with`, an `on_hold` entry wins over an incomplete plan: it is kept in `pending` and put in the held list first, so it is never listed as 'lacking'. `Drain::prepare` does not read an on-hold item to fill its plan.
decisions.reason: The operator sees 'on hold', the actionable reason. A held item must not cost a reader call (drain.rs:2243-2266 would read it otherwise).

rejected.option: Hold only entries whose plan is complete.
rejected.why: An unread held item would be read and charged against the budget, and shown as 'lacking' instead of 'on hold'.

decisions.choice: Show the hold in `athena status` through a new `JobLine.on_hold: bool` (serde skipped when false) and an ' · on hold' suffix in `plan_suffix`. It is a new field, not the existing `JobLine.hold`, which means a disk-space hold.
decisions.reason: The operator needs to see held items in the open-work list. status.rs and display.rs are deliverables. Reusing `hold: Option<String>` would print '(still queued)' text that means something else (display.rs:1068).

rejected.why: Held jobs would look the same as queued ones there, and the operator would not know why drain skips them.

Update the doc comments; add unit tests for the four priorities, the lone low-priority item and the dependent.
Add `Athena::set_hold` and `Athena::release_hold`, modeled on `set_priority` (queued-only check, hold and release checks, next `n`, a records-only commit with an Athena-Job trailer).

Show ' · on hold' in `plan_suffix`; add `on_hold: false` to the two `JobLine` test literals; add a display test for the `held` line with the on-hold reason.
Add `JobLine.on_hold` (skipped when false), set from `job.on_hold()` in `job_line`, and a status test.
Add the tests for criteria 1-5 and 7: Stub drain tests, real-steps drain and plan tests, the real-binary hold and release test, and the help test.
Add an entry under Unreleased / Added.

risks.risk: A drain whose only queued items are all held might not end cleanly or might spin. I read `batches_for` (drain.rs:3034), which drops refused items, but did not trace the whole loop's end condition.
risks.mitigation: The real-steps test asserts the drain returns with no jobs run and no landing. Paused items, which sit in `plan.refused` the same way, already end a drain, and tests/drain.rs:995 and 1332 cover them.

risks.risk: `docs/records.md` is not in the brief's deliverable list. `docs/ontology.toml:56` checks that file for a wording marker.

risks.risk: A hold on a job that is later read with `athena go` is ignored, because `on_hold()` needs the Queued state.
risks.mitigation: This is deliberate (see decisions). `go` is an explicit operator act and drain would otherwise be blocked on a hold the operator can no longer release. A test covers a released and a read job showing no hold.

demonstrations.method: Run the three recorded checks on the final tree. Existing tests are not edited except for adding `on_hold: false` where a struct literal lists every field.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
